title: infrastructure weekly update - 2026-04-13
content:
Overview:
This week (Apr 6–Apr 12) focused on short-term capacity headroom, preparing for the upcoming product spike in mid-May, and triaging a small EU autoscaler regression. We continued the procurement evaluation (H100 vs A100 80GB) and landed a short-term mitigation plan for Dedicated customers that need guaranteed SLAs during the May launch.

High-level status:
- Fleet size (global): 320 GPUs (pilot + prod pools). Regional breakdown: US-West 120, US-East 100, EU-West 70, APAC 30.
- Average fleet utilization (prod pools): 68% this week (target 60–70%). Peak 1-min utilization reached 92% in US-West during Tuesday afternoon burst.
- Pending capacity request: +96 GPUs (expected delivery window: late May if order placed this week).
- Autoscale stability: Mostly stable except EU-West autoscaler bug (see Incident section).

Highlights / Wins:
- Rolled out new batching config for short-chat workloads that reduced per-token cost by ~12% (A/B on prod-route chat-short).
- Completed validation tests for trimmed KV-cache optimization; early results show 8–10% latency reduction for long-sequence generations.
- SRE/infra agreed on emergency reservation policy for Dedicated customers: can carve up to 40 GPUs from the shared pool for 48-hour windows with manual sign-off (docs linked).

GPU Fleet Details:
- Hardware mix under evaluation: A100 80GB (current majority) vs H100 (benchmarks ongoing). H100 shows ~20% lower latency for decoder-only workloads but higher variance with some attention patterns. Price + availability still favor A100 for immediate orders.
- Node health: 2 nodes in US-East flagged for NVMe wear; scheduled maintenance Wed 4/15 02:00–04:00 UTC (no planned customer-impact; will migrate pods first).
- Spot / preemptible pools: Using spot for non-critical batch scoring. Spot preempt rate increased 18% this week in APAC (region-supplier issue). We throttled some background jobs to cope and notified relevant teams.

Regions / Routing / Capacity Allocation:
- Smart routing adjustments deployed: low-latency routing will now prefer US-West -> US-East only if estimated latency < 30ms; otherwise route to EU-West for EU traffic. This reduced cross-region egress by ~9% in the trial.
- Dedicated customers: two customers on reserved pools had near-capacity during Tue peak — we applied temporary carveouts from shared pool to preserve latency SLA. Follow-up: evaluate stricter commit levels or temporary throttles next month.

Capacity Planning / Forecast:
- Demand drivers: May product launch (customer XYZ onboarding), expected +25–35% token throughput for 2–3 weeks.
- Short-term plan: Order +96 A100 80GB immediately (lead time ~6 weeks) to add ~30% headroom to prod pool. Finance pre-approval pending.
- Medium-term: If H100 supply stabilizes and pricing becomes favorable, plan a 50/50 split for new procurement to diversify performance profile.

Incident (EU-West autoscaler regression) — Apr 8
- Summary: Autoscaler policy mis-evaluated spot eviction signals and scaled in aggressively, causing a customer-visible cold-start surge (~120–180s) for some chat requests.
- Impact: ~7% of requests in EU-West experienced degraded latency for ~30 minutes before rollback. No data loss.
- Root cause: Upstream metric (node_eviction_rate) was emitted with an incorrect unit after a metrics SDK bump (PR #982). Autoscaler threshold math misinterpreted the spike.
- Mitigation: Rolled back the metrics SDK change, forced a manual scale-up to replenish pool, and added a short-term guardrail in the autoscaler to ignore single-sample spikes.
- Follow-ups: JIRA-INFRA-4321 to add unit tests + better instrumentation; JIRA-INFRA-4387 to add 3-sample median smoothing in autoscaler.

Standup / Daily notes (week):
- Mon 4/6: Focused on batching rollout QA; flagged KV-cache regression on long sequences.
- Tue 4/7: Apr spike replay test hit peak utilization; throttled background batch jobs to avoid customer impact.
- Wed 4/8: EU autoscaler incident; rolled back metrics SDK change and performed emergency scale-up.
- Thu 4/9: Node maintenance prep for US-East NVMe replacement; started procurement quotes.
- Fri 4/10: Capacity planning readout with product/Sales; finance follow-up for purchase approval.

Action items & owners:
- Alex K: Submit purchase order for +96 A100s once finance OK (due 2026-04-16).
- Priya P: Complete H100 vs A100 benchmark matrix and recommendation doc (due 2026-04-20).
- Michael C: Implement autoscaler median smoothing + unit tests (JIRA-INFRA-4387) (due 2026-04-17).
- Sofia R: Coordinate maintenance window communication for US-East (completed).
- Jordan L: Update runbook for emergency reservations and publish to Confluence (due 2026-04-15).

Blockers / Risks:
- Procurement lead times could push delivery into June if the order is delayed; that would leave us exposed during the May spike.
- Spot availability in APAC remains volatile; consider temporarily moving some background workloads to EU or US pools.
- H100 supply/pricing uncertainty: need final benchmark + price quote to decide by next week.

Meetings / Syncs next week:
- Mon 4/13 10:00 UTC: Capacity planning review with Product & Finance (Alex, Priya).
- Tue 4/14 16:00 UTC: Autoscaler postmortem + fixes review (Michael, SRE team).
- Thu 4/16 09:00 UTC: Dedicated customer SLA carveout dry run (SRE + Customer Success).

Notes / Misc:
- Small housekeeping: Renamed internal pool tags for easier billing allocation (prod-usw, prod-use, prod-euw, prod-apac). Update your stack configs if you reference old tags.
- Saved benchmark artifacts and raw traces to the Confluence page linked above.

TL;DR: Fleet stable overall; we hit a short-lived autoscaler bug in EU-West but mitigated quickly. Recommend approval to order +96 A100s to cover May launch risk. Action owners noted above — please update JIRA items as you progress.
